{{Short description|On existence of a continuous function between semicontinuous upper and lower bounds}}

The '''Katětov–Tong insertion theorem'''<ref>Miroslav Katětov, ''On real-valued functions in topological spaces'', Fundamenta Mathematicae 38(1951), 85–91. [http://pldml.icm.edu.pl/pldml/element/bwmeta1.element.bwnjournal-article-fmv38i1p9]; ''Correction to "On real-valued functions in topological spaces"'', Fundamenta Mathematicae 40(1953), 203–205. [http://pldml.icm.edu.pl/pldml/element/bwmeta1.element.bwnjournal-article-fmv40i1p22]</ref><ref>Hing Tong, ''Some characterizations of normal and perfectly normal spaces'', Duke Mathematical Journal 19(1952), 289–292. {{doi|10.1215/S0012-7094-52-01928-5}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Good |first1=Chris |last2=Stares |first2=Ian |title=New proofs of classical insertion theorems |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/255580849}}</ref> is a theorem of [[point-set topology]] proved independently by [[Miroslav Katětov]] and [[Hing Tong]] in the 1950s.  The theorem states the following:

Let <math>X</math> be a [[normal space|normal]] [[topological space]] and let <math>g, h\colon X \to \mathbb{R}</math> be functions with <math>g</math> upper [[semicontinuous]], <math>h</math> lower semicontinuous, and <math>g \leq h</math>. Then there exists a continuous function <math>f\colon X \to \mathbb{R}</math> with <math>g \leq f \leq h.</math>

This theorem has a number of applications and is the first of many classical insertion theorems. In particular it implies the [[Tietze extension theorem]] and consequently [[Urysohn's lemma]], and so the conclusion of the theorem is equivalent to normality.
